name: Lewis Rotating Cylinder
description: The stationary vacuum fields with cylindrical symmetry, the space outside an infinitely long rotating cylinder, which Thomas Lewis wrote down in 1932. With real constants the field is locally Levi-Civita's static one and the rotation shows only on a trip round the axis; with an imaginary exponent it is static nowhere. Both kinds hold the vacuum outside van Stockum's cylinder of dust.
convention: We keep factors of $c$ explicit, and the Ricci tensor is the standard contraction, $R_{\mu\nu} = R^\alpha{}_{\mu\alpha\nu}$.
history: What does spacetime look like outside an infinitely long cylinder that spins? For a cylinder at rest Tullio Levi-Civita had the answer by 1919 [levicivita1919]. The spinning one came out in 1932, when Thomas Lewis published what he called "some special, but exact, solutions which the author obtained some years ago" [lewis1932]. A stationary field of the same kind had served Kornel Lanczos for a cosmology in 1924, as Lewis himself noted, and the two are credited with finding it independently [lanczos1924, lewis1932, bronnikov2020]. Lewis's family is the general stationary vacuum solution with cylindrical symmetry, built from four constants $n$, $a$, $b$, and $q$ [costa2021, dasilva1995weyl].¶The family found its cylinder in 1937, when Willem Jacob van Stockum solved a cylinder of dust in rigid rotation and joined Lewis's vacuum to it smoothly [vanstockum1937, costa2021]. The vacuum outside comes in three kinds, sorted by the product of the dust's angular velocity $w$ and the cylinder's radius $R$ [bonnor1980, bronnikov2020]. Below $wR = 1/2$ all four of Lewis's constants are real, which is called the Weyl class [costa2021, dasilva1995weyl]. Above it $n$ is imaginary, the powers of $r$ become cosines and sines of $\ln r$, and the solution belongs to the Lewis class [costa2021, dasilva1995lewis]. Around a rapidly rotating cylinder Frank Tipler found, in 1974, closed timelike lines joining any two events [tipler1974].¶The Weyl class hides its spin well: a new time, $\tau = \sqrt{a}\,(t + b\phi/c)$, with a matching change of the angle, turns Lewis's metric into Levi-Civita's static one [bronnikov2020]. M. F. A. da Silva, Luis Herrera, Filipe Paiva, and Nilton Santos proved in 1995, with the Cartan scalars, that the two have the same curvature at every point, and that $n$ alone curves the spacetime [dasilva1995weyl, bronnikov2020]. So where did the rotation go? It went into the angle: $\phi$ and $\phi + 2\pi$ are one place, so a lap of the cylinder brings $\tau$ back shifted by $2\pi\sqrt{a}\,b/c$ unless $b = 0$ [bronnikov2020]. Picture a parking garage, where every floor is level and one lap of the ramp still leaves you a storey up. John Stachel's phrase for such a spacetime, from 1982, is globally stationary but locally static, and he called it a gravitational analog of the Aharonov-Bohm effect [stachel1982].¶By 1998 Malcolm MacCallum and Santos had cut the four constants to three: one fixes the local gravitational field, and two record how the angle is closed up to make a cylinder [maccallum1998]. The three turned up in 2021, when L. Filipe O. Costa, José Natário, and Santos set Lewis's coordinates turning rigidly until they stood fixed to the distant stars [costa2021]. In that frame the metric holds the Komar mass per unit length $\sigma$, the angular momentum per unit length $j$, and the angle deficit, and $\partial_t$ is timelike at every radius [costa2021]. It is Levi-Civita's metric with $c\,dt + 4j\,d\phi/(1 - 4\sigma)$ in the place of $c\,dt$ [costa2021]. Light sent both ways round a loop of fibre comes back a fixed time apart if the loop encloses the cylinder, whatever its shape, and together if it does not: a Sagnac effect that plays the part of Aharonov and Bohm's [costa2021].¶The Lewis class is another animal: it is static in no coordinates, even locally, it has no flat member, and its curvature differs from Levi-Civita's [dasilva1995lewis, costa2021]. Its Kretschmann scalar is Lewis's with $n = im$, positive only while $m < \sqrt{3}$ [costa2021]. Back in the Weyl class, $n = 1$ is flat: with $b = q = 0$ it is the cone round a cosmic string, and with $b$ alone the string spins, its angular momentum set by $b\sqrt{a}$ [bronnikov2020, jensen1992]. Exchange $z$ and $\phi$ and Lewis's metric is the field of a cylinder sliding along its own axis, which Kirill Bronnikov, Santos, and Anzhong Wang wrote in 2020 "has not been studied in detail" [bronnikov2020].

related.text: Lewis's cylinder with the spin taken away. At $b = q = 0$ the metric is Levi-Civita's, with $\sigma = (1 - n)/4$, and the whole Weyl class is locally that static field [bronnikov2020, dasilva1995weyl].

The cylinder of dust in rigid rotation that Lewis's vacuum surrounds. Willem Jacob van Stockum joined the two in 1937, and the vacuum is of the Weyl class for $wR < 1/2$ and of the Lewis class for $wR > 1/2$ [vanstockum1937, costa2021].
The flat member that still spins. At $n = 1$ and $q = 0$ Lewis's metric is the spinning cosmic string, with angular momentum set by $b\sqrt{a}$ [bronnikov2020, jensen1992].
The flat member at rest. At $n = 1$ and $b = q = 0$ only the cone is left, with $a$ setting the missing angle [bronnikov2020].

The Lewis class at $m = \sqrt{3}$, where the Kretschmann scalar vanishes. There the field gains a fourth symmetry and is Petrov's homogeneous vacuum, the same at every event [bonnor1979petrov, bonnor1980].
A cylinder of shearing, rotating dust with Lewis's vacuum around it. R. Chan and N. O. Santos showed that only the Weyl class of the family joins to such dust [bonnor2009maitra, chan2024].

parameters.description: Lewis's exponent, real and positive in the Weyl class; it is the one constant the curvature depends on, and $\sigma = (1 - n)/4$ is the mass parameter of Levi-Civita's cylinder
Lewis's constant $a$, a positive number; without rotation it sets the angular deficit about the axis
Lewis's constant $b$, a length; with $q = 0$ it is the time, as a length, by which a circuit of the axis shifts the static time $t + b\phi/c$
Lewis's constant $c$, a number, which measures the rotation of the source; with $b = q = 0$ the metric is Levi-Civita's
Unit of length for $r$, the scale Lewis's dimensionless coordinates leave implicit
The power of the radius the three functions of Lewis's metric are built from
Lewis's $e^\mu$, the coefficient of $dr^2 + dz^2$
Lewis's $f$, minus the norm of $\partial_t$, which is negative beyond $u = na/q$
Lewis's $k = -Af$, with $A = q\,r\,u/(n\,a\,f) + b$
Lewis's $l = r^2/f - A^2f$, the norm of $\partial_\phi$, so that $fl + k^2 = r^2$

coordinates.convention: We use Lewis's coordinates $(t, r, \phi, z)$ with all four of his constants real, the Weyl class, and $t$ carrying dimensions of time, $r$ and $z$ lengths, and $\phi$ periodic in $2\pi$. We write $q$ for the constant the literature calls $c$, and measure $r$ in a length $\ell$, so that $u$ and $h$ are pure numbers. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.
